description:
FILED s1061 (Opus, 2026-09-07) from #1061's CPAN-board bisects.  Residue of
#199/#201 (Capture-Tiny), and the mechanism is general.

THE MECHANISM.  PCL parses `f { BLOCK } LIST` as a block-form call only when
it knows f's prototype starts with `&`, and it learns prototypes by SCANNING
THE MODULE SOURCE for a literal `sub NAME (PROTO)`
(Pl::Parser::_extract_module_prototypes / _merge_module_prototypes).
Capture::Tiny does not write one.  Its four exported subs are built in a
loop:

    lib/Capture/Tiny.pm:38
      eval "sub $sub(&;@) {unshift \@_, $args; goto \\&_capture_tee;}";

so there is no literal to find, the caller's `capture { … }` is not a
block-form call, and the statement DROPS (`;; PARSE ERROR: Bug. Fell
through. Missing case: [...]`).  perl has no such problem: `use Capture::Tiny`
runs that eval at COMPILE time, before the caller's body is compiled.

This is the same family as #478 (the prototype pre-scan skipping Test2::/
Test:: modules BY NAME) but a different cause: there the literal exists and is
skipped, here there is no literal at all.

BOARD COST, and why it changed shape.  The four drops are old; what changed is
their PRICE.  At `f702da31` (s435, THE FLIP) a dropped statement stopped being
a silent `nil` and became a run-time die, and its loss unit is the enclosing
TOP-LEVEL FORM (#1433) -- which, in a test file that opens with `my $Builder`
or `my $fd`, is the rest of the file.  So four Capture-Tiny files went from
PARTIAL to FAIL 0/0 between the s378 and s467 board snapshots:

    09-preserve-exit-code.t  PARTIAL 1/1   -> FAIL 0/0   (1 drop,  line 22)
    17-pass-results.t        PARTIAL 1/11  -> FAIL 0/0   (4 drops, lines 30/44/58/70)
    19-relayering.t          PARTIAL 3/2   -> FAIL 0/0   (1 drop,  line 63)
    25-cap-fork.t            PARTIAL 1/2   -> FAIL 0/0   (1 drop,  line 31)

Verified: the s378 tree (`5d941618`) emits the SAME drops, as
`(progn ;; PARSE ERROR … nil)`.  Real perl 5.40.3 passes all four files
(2/12/5/4 rows).  This is the flip working as ruled -- the loud price of a
compiler gap -- so the board rows are EXPECTED, and this task is the gap.

NOT IN THE DROP CENSUS.  `baselines/parse-error-drop-census-s399.tsv` has no
Capture-Tiny rows: its cpan population is `cpan-tests/modules/**/t/**`, and
the 14-dist BOARD's own `t/` files are in no census population at all.  Seven
drops in four files of one board dist, invisible to every counter.  Worth
folding into #1502/#1504's board work.

FIX SHAPES, in order of how much they change:
  (a) declare the four in a `lib/Capture/Tiny.pm` shim -- the LAYER-correct
      one-module answer (CLAUDE.md 9a), and it is what `lib/List/Util.pm`
      already does for `first (&@)`;
  (b) teach the module prototype scan to read `eval "sub NAME(PROTO)"` --
      generic, but it is a text scan of a string literal;
  (c) make a module's compile phase actually RUN before a caller that `use`s
      it is parsed -- the honest answer, and the largest.
subject: A prototype installed by a STRING EVAL in a module is invisible to the caller's block-form parse: Capture::Tiny builds `sub capture(&;@)` with `eval "sub $sub(&;@) {…}"`, so `capture { … }` is a DROP -- four board files that were PARTIAL are FAIL 0/0 since the flip
